2. Respondents above named filed the above aforesaid S.C.C. suit against the appellant and respondent No. 4 for eviction from the suit premises and obtained a decree for eviction. The decree was put to execution when it was found that the suit premises was wrongly shown as plot 4314 in the schedule of the plaint although in the body of the plaint it was shown as 4313. The respondents filed application for correction of the aforesaid plot as 4313 instead of plot No. 4514. The learned S.C.C. Judge rejected the application for correction on the ground that the court had become functus officio. 

 3. The plaintiff then moved the High Court Division and the prayer for correction was allowed under Sections 151, 152 and 153 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Being aggrieved by the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division the appellant filed the petition for leave to appeal which was granted to consider whether the High Court Division acted wrongly and illegally in allowing the correction of the decree under Sections 152 and 153 of the Code of Civil Procedure which resulted in correction of the plaint which is riot amendable under Sections 152 and 153 of the Code." It is submitted on behalf of the appellant that the order passed by the High Court Division is in effect an order under Order 6 Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the provision of Sections 151, 152 and 153 of he Code of Civil Procedure have no manner of application in the facts and circumstances of the case. It is further contended that the High Court Division has no jurisdiction in revision in allowing amendment of the decree in substituting one plot by another and the same amendments can only be caused by amendment under Order 6 Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure by the trial court and there is no scope to be had from evidence as to whether the plaintiff has got right to claim eviction from the plot now claimed by him. On the other hand it is argued arid submitted on behalf of the respondent that the defendant appellant having not challenged the identity of the snit land at any stage of the litigation, the High Court Division committed no error in allowing the application of the plaintiff respondent for correction of the plot number. It was also clear that it was a bonafide case of clerical error or typing mistake and therefore the High Court Division rightly allowed correction under the provisions of Sections 151, 152 and 153 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The question therefore is whether the amendment asked for by the plaintiff respondent before the court was of a, formal nature in that it was for correction to a typing error or that it was an amendment of the plaint which can only be done under Order 6 Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the first paragraph of the plaint the plaintiff-respondent contended he gave lease of the premises in plot. No. 4313 for running of a Karunamayee Hindu Hotel but in the schedule the plot number is mentioned as 4313. The first paragraph of plaint reads as follows: 

 Admittedly there was a tenancy agreement between them and there has been no averment denying this statement made in the plaint. The identity of the premises was not challenged by the defendant-appellant at any stage of the trial Further a copy of the tenancy agreement was submitted which show that the premises rented out was plot No. 4313 and therefore the mentioning of plot No. 4314 in the schedule of the plain is obviously a typing error. The High Court Division also found that plot No. 4314 in (he schedule was a typing error. The amendment sought being of the formal nature it falls within Section 151, 152 and 153 of the Code of Civil Procedure which (he court can correct. The High Court Division therefore held that such correction of clerical mistake does riot amount to amendment of the plaint under Order 6 Rule 17. In the circumstances we do not find any illegality in the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in allowing the correction in the schedule of the plaint by substituting plot No. 4313 in place of 4314. It may be noted that the premises which was rented has been described as holding No. 94 of Central Road, Nababgonj Bazar, Rangpur Town which further identifies the premises from which the plaintiff respondent sought eviction of the defendant appellant.
